segments.he: גְּמָ׳ לִמְקוֹם שֶׁרִיבָּה אִין, לִמְקוֹם שֶׁמִּיעֵט לָא? אֵימָא: אַף לִמְקוֹם שֶׁרִיבָּה.
segments.en: «GEMARA:» The Gemara asks: Does this mean that in «a place where he extended» the limit, «yes,» the surveyor’s measurements are accepted, but in «a place where he reduced» the limit, «no,» his measurements are not accepted? If his extended measurement is accepted, his shortened measurement should certainly be accepted as well. The Gemara answers: «Say» that the mishna means that the surveyor’s measurements are accepted «even» in «a place where he extended» the limit, without concern that he might have erred (Tosafot), and that the surveyor’s measurements are certainly accepted in places where he reduced the Shabbat limit.

moves.summary: does the mishna exclude the reduced measurement?
moves.about: the mishna implies a reduced measurement is not followed, though it is certainly included
